subject: Re: Pro-rata availability calculation & monthly credit approach
messages:
From: Rebecca Zhang <rzhang@tidaltech.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: operations@tidaltech.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: SLA redlines — calculating availability and monthly credits

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and procurement teams reviewed the standard SLA and came back with a handful of redlines focused on how availability is calculated and how credits are issued. Two asks in particular are blocking approval:

1) Pro-rata calculation for partial-day degradations — we run time-sensitive pipelines and a 3-hour partial outage should not be treated the same as a full-day outage. We want credits to be proportional to minutes of degraded availability rather than broad monthly bands.

2) Monthly credit cap — instead of a fixed dollar cap, we'd prefer a cap expressed as a percentage of the monthly invoice (they suggested 50%) to ensure economics scale with usage.

We also asked for a clear rule about scheduled maintenance windows: specifically, maintenance under 2 hours/month should be excluded from uptime calculations; anything longer should be notified with a 7-day window and have a make-good mechanism.

I've attached our redlines (Tidal_SLA_Redlines_v1.docx) so you can see exact language. Can you confirm whether Redwood would consider a pro-rata minutes-based methodology and a usage-relative credit cap? If not, what alternatives do you recommend?

Happy to hop on a quick call this week.

Best,
Rebecca Zhang
Head of Ops, TidalTech
rebecca.zhang@tidaltech.com
Attachments: Tidal_SLA_Redlines_v1.docx (docx)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rebecca Zhang <rzhang@tidaltech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA redlines — calculating availability and monthly credits

Hi Rebecca —

Appreciate the detailed redlines and the clarity on what your procurement team needs. I've reviewed the doc and pulled together a short counterproposal for how we can meet you in the middle without exposing Redwood to open-ended credit liability. High-level thoughts:

- Pro-rata (minutes-based) credits: We can implement a minutes-proportional credit calculation for incidents that meet our definition of "Service Degraded" vs "Service Unavailable." Practically: credits would be (minutes_of_degraded_service / total_minutes_in_billing_period) * monthly_invoice. This gives you the proportionality you requested while tying it to your actual spend.

- Credit cap as percentage of invoice: We can agree to a cap expressed as a percent of the monthly invoice rather than a fixed dollar amount. Our legal/commercial team prefers a top-line cap to protect rare corner cases; we'd be comfortable with a 30% monthly invoice cap as a starting point and open to escalation paths if there’s a pattern of recurring failures.

- Scheduled maintenance: we can exclude up to 2 hours/month if notified 72 hours in advance. For maintenance longer than 2 hours, we will provide a mitigation plan and will not count the time against availability if an alternative region/replica is used; otherwise we will treat it as scheduled and not eligible for credits if advance notice provided.

- Latency SLOs: separate layer — if you need a latency credit tied to p95/p99, we can add a latency SLO and a smaller, distinct credit pool.

I've attached a short counterproposal (RW_Counterproposal_pro-rata_v1.docx) with suggested contract language. Laura — can you please flag any legal showstoppers on the minutes-based formula and the 30% cap? Ben — happy to align on commercial flexibility here; Rebecca, would you be open to a brief call Friday to finalize?

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Cc: operations@tidaltech.com

Subject: Re: SLA redlines — calculating availability and monthly credits

Sofia,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear proposal. A couple of clarifications from our side before we lock a call:

- Minutes-based credits: that formula looks good conceptually. Procurement will want to see worked examples (e.g., 3h partial outage in a 30-day billing period on a $120k monthly invoice => what credit). Could you add an appendix with two worked examples?

- Cap: 30% as a starting point is reasonable, thank you for that. Our CFO is hesitant on a hard cap that could trigger us to accept systemic issues; she prefers the 50% suggestion but is willing to consider 30% if we also put in an "escalation window": if a customer receives >30% credits two months in a rolling six-month window, then both parties enter a remediation/credits-escrow discussion with a predefined remediation plan.

- Latency: we do want a p95 target (100ms) with a small separate credit band; attaching our measured latency histogram for the week of Apr 4–11 for context.

If you can add worked examples and the escalation clause language, I think procurement and legal will be able to move quickly. Call Friday still works for us — available 11:00–13:00 PT.

Best,
Rebecca
Attachments: latency_histogram_apr-week.png (png)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Thanks Rebecca — this all sounds workable.

Quick notes: 1) We'll add two worked examples to the next draft and include the escalation trigger language you proposed (">30% credits in 2 of rolling 6 months" => remediation window). 2) For the latency p95 band we'll propose a smaller credit pool (max 8% of monthly invoice) separate from availability credits. 3) We'll also include a short definition table to clarify "Service Degraded" vs "Service Unavailable."

Sofia — I'll join Friday at 11:30 PT and Laura, please confirm signoff on the 30% cap with escalation path (not a legal blocker for negotiation). Rebecca — we'll send updated redline and examples by EOD Thursday so you have time to review before Friday.

Cheers,
